contentPath: apps/garden/content/Keep your notes in the repo.md
reviewer: Author's editorial pass, 2026-09-18: research subagents fetched and quoted each source; every quoted passage was re-fetched independently and matched verbatim before scoring. First-person incident notes; external sources ground the mechanisms named, not the incidents themselves.
reviewNotes: Original contribution is the source-versus-derived-index framing and the explicit conditions under which a database is the right call. Removed the unsupported line that search engines prefer static output. Tool references are to their own documentation. Limits section bounds the claim to a small single-author corpus.

claims.text: Tools like [Quartz](https://quartz.jzhao.xyz/features/obsidian-compatibility) exist precisely to publish a vault as a static site
claims.sourcePassage: Quartz was originally designed as a tool to publish Obsidian vaults as websites.
claims.limitation: One tool's self-description; not a survey of static site generators.

claims.text: A static build [writes one HTML file per route](https://nextjs.org/docs/app/guides/static-exports)
claims.sourcePassage: When running next build, Next.js generates an HTML file per route.
claims.limitation: Framework-specific; other generators differ in output shape.

claims.text: [Obsidian's own hosted publishing](https://obsidian.md/publish), which charges per site per month
claims.sourcePassage: Per site, per month, billed annually
claims.limitation: Vendor pricing page; amounts change and are deliberately not quoted in the note.

claims.text: Source of truth in plain files under version control. Derived indexes wherever they earn their place. Never the other way round.
claims.rationale: Author's architectural rule; the Limits section bounds it to small single-author corpora.
